findings.issue: Sea Glass is the answer, yet it is the only dairy-free venue without a clear no-milk statement. Lantern Pier says 'no cow's milk in the place', Pelican Steps 'you won't find a carton of milk', Low Tide 'no milk or butter anywhere', and Kittiwake 'nothing on the board contains milk'. Sea Glass only shows that the creamies use oat milk and coconut, plus 'crates of oat milk... where most parlours keep the milk churns'. Its fruit sorbets are never ruled milk-free, and this level's Sandpiper trap teaches the player exactly that a board saying 'sorbet' can hide milk. So a careful player has good reason to doubt the answer's dairy status. Gabriella also asked for this evidence to be clear.
findings.rule: Critic brief check 2 (every deciding attribute evident from reviews alone); map-seeder brief: 'The evidence must still be unambiguous to a careful reader'
findings.suggested_fix: In review 2, replace the final sentence 'A gull has learned to wait on the railing for dropped cones.' with: 'My cousin can't have cow's milk, and she worked her way through both halves of the board, sorbets and creamies, with a perfectly happy stomach all the way home. On Fridays the owner chalks the tide times up next to the flavours.'

findings.where: script[15] (Brooke: 'tonight i want light and fresh, not a dessert stacked on top of a dessert')

findings.rule: Narrative-writer brief, Reserved and pinned details: 'In implied and buried levels, don't reuse a character's earlier stated-level wording for their need'; bible clue rule 5 (clue style)
findings.suggested_fix: script[15]: 'i can still feel it. tonight i want something that tastes mostly of fruit, not a dessert stacked on top of a dessert' (NEUTRAL, clue vibe:healthy). Every review can confirm or rule this out: the fruit-forward cups at Sea Glass, Pelican Steps, Sandpiper, Lantern Pier and Kittiwake versus Low Tide's doughnut sundae and syrup-soaked waffle.

findings.where: script[16]-[20] (Roxy's sherbet system, Cyrus's sherbet/sorbet lesson, Roxy, Maya, Roxy)

findings.issue: Three reviews rest on a staff assurance: Low Tide quotes the owner, Pelican Steps reports a booking-form reply, and Anchor Lane reports a kitchen note. The brief allows at most one staff promise per level, and the form reply and kitchen note share a shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the first two sentences of Anchor Lane review 2 with: 'My girlfriend carries an allergy pen and has eaten here every Sunday since spring without a single scare; the fryer only ever sees olive oil, and there isn't a peanut on the premises.' Keep the rest of the review (sorbetto, cherries, cat) as written.

summary: A strong buried opener for chapter 4. The craving (Liam's dropped-cone story), outdoor seating ('not spending it under a ceiling', which fits Liam's love of patios in the cast table), healthy (the housewarming) and peanut (Roxy's 'every topping' prompting Cyrus) all come out of other talk mid-conversation. The promotion beat delivers the $$ restatement in Maya's voice and makes Pelican Steps a clear one-star sigh. The two must-fixes: Sea Glass is the only dairy-free venue without an unambiguous no-milk line, at the exact point where the Sandpiper trap teaches distrust of 'sorbet' labels; and Brooke's healthy wish reuses her stated-level 'light and fresh'. The dairy block is heavier than a buried level needs. Note also that the seeder's missing vegan_options tags don't matter: no guest in the campaign is vegan and players never see tags.
